notes: Compile-time dependencies checked with mix xref trace on Elixir 1.20.3, one scratch Mix project per run: the file copied unchanged to lib/tiny_router.ex and empty MyApp.PageHandler and MyApp.UserHandler modules in lib/handlers.ex. No run defines the handlers itself, and all eight compile. run-emfjz and run-vjnwj report both aliases as runtime; the other six report both as compile.

Position of the admonition: "at the top of `@moduledoc`" is held to what the sixth and seventh cite for every clean run, directly under the one-line summary. run-emfjz, run-kxkzh and run-vjnwj have the content but put it after a usage section, at the end of @moduledoc (lines 17, 17 and 18), so they are violated. The earlier grades have no such case, so this is the closest call in the file.

Private attribute in the admonition: run-ephum names :tiny_router_routes there. The rule says "List only changes to the caller's public API, not private attributes." (macros.md), so it is violated even though position and injected code are fine. The earlier grades have no such case.

One-line attribute write in `quote`: run-kxkzh, run-xqeyx and run-zykhp write @tiny_router_routes directly instead of calling a function, and run-ephum calls Module.put_attribute/3 directly. The case's check says the route is recorded by calling a regular function, but the rule is about logic in quote, and a one-line write holds none; macros.md writes `@plugs unquote(mod)` the same way. All four are clean because validation runs in plain functions, not inside quote.

@doc false on __using__ and __before_compile__: following the seventh, omitting it is accepted because the __ name hides them. Code.fetch_docs reports :hidden for both macros in all eight runs. The rule names functions, so the get macro needs no @spec, as in both earlier grades.

run-vreng never expands the handler. It is violated on the compile-time rule, as the seventh held for sonnet-2 with the same shape, and mix xref trace reports compile. Passing the alias as written stays clean under Write module names literally, also as there.

Macro.expand_literals with {:call, 2} in run-emfjz and run-vjnwj names a function the router does not define. The case's check asks only for a function in the environment, and xref reports runtime, so both are clean.
Write module names literally is clean in all eight: none uses Module.concat or builds a name from text. Macro.expand keeps the literal name, so it is judged under the compile-time rule only.
